title: Leave the World Behind (2023) or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Binge.

commenti.body:
>Mozzarella Ali

Well, I guess I don't need to take anything else in this "post" seriously. Good god. 

Also... it's *rogue*, not *rouge*. *Rouge* is french for "red", or a given scoring play in the CFL, learn the fucking difference. 

What a lazy, pointless "review". Imagine thinking that this film's central thesis is "buy DVDs" and not, I dunno, misanthropism leads to societal weakness and an eventual breakdown. 

That all said, the film's *whole point* is that there is no "central explanation of what is going on". It's about uncertainty and despair and the whole psychological effect of suddenly being in a world where at one point *everything* was known and the second it's not (due to a cyberattack) makes it all worse. 

Tell me you have no idea what a film is about without telling me you have no idea what a film is about.

What does this have to do with binging content?

It is a single movie.

My take:
The storyline  is not very surprising or novel. I agree on that. But! It has amazing camerawork, really nice shots. Those are worth the watch already.

I was also pleasantly surprised by Julia Roberts, who plays an unpleasant tormented and aging woman very well. 

The other cast also did a good job, I liked the alienated little girl.

For the Mr Robot afficionados there are supposedly some easter eggs. The mystery of this movie makes a bit more sense if you have seen the series. 

I do not mind the open ended story and unanswered questions.

As for the morale, I can only agree...
Ahhhh, so this is why people find this sub pretentious.

I very much disagree on the "amazing camerawork" bit, even if you like the director's shots on Mr. Robot and Homecoming.

In this film, I think he was at his worst: I can't remember every single instance, but I recall the stupid zoom-ins in the characters' face (I know he was indeed aiming for a comical effect, but the execution was awful and so in your face) and that interesting top-down, spinning shot of the cabin that was absolutely wasted by just showing ONE random deer running.

Many times he would explore a different perspective, only to then not take advantage of those. It felt really frustrating.

The movies is awful and basically a Netflix spot. However anyone having faith for esmaili forgets that Mr robot is a four season nothing burger filled with populist rethoric and style over substance constantly. This movie is so flat that I was almost shocked at how he didn't even bother to try and make something interesting or valid. The most garbage Netflix movie since bird box/death note.

Every single change of perspective amounted to absolutely nothing in a way that it's off putting. And I don't think it was thought that way, but rather "oh let's create the coolest shot for no reason or thought behind it, it worked with Mr robot"
What's pretentious about anything I said, exactly? I'd love a detailed explanation.
What a surprise, you can't. Classic troll play of people who throw around the word "pretentious".
